newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk traders to demonstrate against Iraqi embargo.
newsitem.headline: Turk traders to demonstrate against Iraqi embargo.

text.p: Traders in southeastern Turkey will hold a demonstration at the weekend to urge the United Nations to end the trade embargo against Iraq, their association said on Tuesday.

"It is evident that the embargo did not yield any benefit apart from making the oppressed people of Iraq and millions of people living in eastern and southeastern Turkey miserable," the Gaziantep Chamber of Trade said in a statement.
The chamber in the southeastern town of Gaziantep is the biggest trade organisation in the region, badly hit by sanctions on Baghdad imposed after its invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
It said the demonstration would be held in Gaziantep on Saturday.
Before the 1990-91 Gulf crisis, Iraq was Turkey's third biggest trade partner. Southeastern and eastern traders had a major stake in the bilateral trade with Iraq.
The chamber said Turkey had to be given "some flexibilities" to ease the difficulties faced by Turks in the region.
U.S. cruise missiles slammed into southern Iraq on Tuesday in retaliation for government troop movements into the rebel north of the country.
